graft.title: design_propose drops a change's unknown fields without saying so (journal text lost)
graft.need: design_propose accepts a change with fields it doesn't know and stores the change without them, reporting success. A `journal` change given its text as `text` (or `lesson`, `alternatives`) instead of `body` was committed and signed with `"body": null`: the entry has a title and nothing else, and the tool's answer ("Committed batch ... Decision: <title>") looks the same as when the text lands. In autodyne on 2026-10-05, four entries (batches 01a10ade-8a1d, 01a10b1f, 01a10e54/01a10e55-b5ac) lost their text this way and were re-recorded with `supersedes` (batch 01a10e56-83b8). Wanted: an unknown field in a change is an error that names the field and the ones the action takes (here: `text` isn't a journal field; did you mean `body`?), or at least a warning in the answer; and the answer echoes how much of the body was stored (e.g. 'Decision: <title> (1,114 chars)') so an empty entry is visible. The same likely applies to other actions (link's `code` vs `path` already errors, which is the behavior wanted everywhere).
graft.use_case: Agents record decisions and missteps as they go (the conduct asks for it); a silently empty entry defeats the journal, and nothing shows it until someone reads the log by hand.

answer.text: Fixed in tend 486176d (deployed). A change naming a field its action doesn't take is refused, saying what the action takes and, for the usual slips, what was meant: `journal takes no 'text' (it takes body, kind, node, rests_on, supersedes, title): did you mean body?`. The fields come from the change language's own reference (ACTIONS), which now lists everything the resolver reads; open ones (a toolbox entry's) aren't checked. design_propose's answer says how much text each journal entry holds ('Decision: … (1114 chars)', or 'no text'), so an empty one shows.
